AI Research - EU Grants Funding Skip to content Download Summary PDF AI research AI Research Currently open AI research grants and funding opportunities Call for applications to support collaborative research projects between Japan and Europe in the field of AI-powered robotics May 04, 2026; Other EU Programmes ; AI Grants , Innovation grants , Research grants Call for research proposals focused on the development of AI-powered robotics. This initiative seeks to fund collaborative projects between researchers in Japan and Europe to create adaptive, autonomous systems capable of functioning in dynamic and human-centered environments. Thte primary goal of this funding is to address complex scientific challenges while delivering tangible solutions to societal needs, such as elderly care, industrial productivity, and disaster response. Proposals may explore a wide range of technologies, including: Machine Learning and Deep Learning (ML/DL); Computer Vision and SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping); Natural Language Processing (NLP) for robot programming; and Human-Robot Interaction and co-manipulation. A total funding pool of EUR 6,370,000 is available to support various costs. Call for applications to support innovative solutions leveraging AI and technology in sustainability, healthcare, robotics, and education May 04, 2026; Non-EU / Global / International Grants ; AI Grants , Education grants , Health Grants , Innovation grants , Sustainability funding Call for applications for an Innovators Pitch, a program dedicated to scaling technological solutions that address the world’s most pressing challenges. With a focus on Sustainability, Health, Robotics, and Education, the initiative seeks projects that leverage artificial intelligence and cutting-edge tech to accelerate progress, such as optimizing energy grids, enhancing precision surgery, or personalizing instruction for under-resourced students. This call comes at a pivotal time, following a 2025 trend where nearly half of global funding was directed toward the AI sector, underscoring the massive potential for AI-enabled innovations to drive human prosperity. Selected innovators will receive significant exposure and support, including the opportunity to pitch their solutions on stage. Beyond the pitch, participants gain privileged access to the investment community, masterclasses designed to expand technical expertise, and a complimentary Institute Membership. By bridging the gap between visionary ideas and the influential changemakers of the ecosystem, the institute aims to transform high-impact technology into scalable, real-world solutions that leave a lasting legacy on humanity. Call for applications to support AI innovators in integrating their mature AI solutions into an AI Platform April 30, 2026; Non-EU / Global / International Grants ; AI Grants , Digital technologies grants , Innovation grants Call for applications aimed at SMEs and research organizations to integrate mature AI solutions into Europe’s leading open AI ecosystem. This initiative seeks to accelerate the deployment of trustworthy, ethical, and transparent AI by funding innovators who can provide impactful solutions for the platform’s Marketplace and Business Navigator. To be eligible, applicants must be registered in an EU Member State or a DIGITAL Europe associated country and possess a product at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7 or above, delivered in a containerized format such as Docker. Selected applicants will enter a competitive three-stage funnel program designed to validate business models and drive platform adoption. The funding is distributed as follows: AI Providers: Eligible for up to €60,000 in lump-sum financial support; AI Adopters: Eligible for up to €15,000 to support the real-world deployment of these solutions. Beyond direct financial support, the program offers a comprehensive suite of resources to ensure the success of integrated solutions. Participants receive expert mentorship to sharpen their business strategies and reduce technical risks. Additionally, the program enhances market visibility by providing innovators with the opportunity to pitch their solutions at up to three major in-person industry events across Europe. By the third stage, AI Providers will form consortia with AI Adopters to demonstrate the practical utility and scalability of their integrated AI products. Call for applications to support AI/ML-focused tech startups in Europe and Israel April 29, 2026; Non-EU / Global / International Grants ; Accelerator programs , AI Grants , Innovation grants Call for applications for a three-month virtual accelerator program, specifically designed for tech startups in Europe and Israel that are leveraging AI to drive the energy transition. The initiative targets companies between the Pre-Seed and Series A+ stages that are developing scalable, deeply technical solutions in areas such as grid modernization, demand flexibility, and energy affordability for both residential and industrial sectors. Selected cohorts of 10 to 15 startups will receive equity-free support, including specialized mentoring, strategic guidance, and technical project partnerships with experts. Beyond human expertise, participants gain significant product advantages, such as early access to AI tools, potential Cloud credits, and free access to Cloud TPUs to accelerate their machine learning research. Interested founders must demonstrate a defensible growth model and ensure a commitment from their technical leadership to engage fully in the program’s workshops and sprint projects. Call for proposals to enhance the security, privacy, and robustness of AI models and systems March 06, 2026; Horizon Europe funding opportunities ; AI Grants , Digital technologies grants , Innovation grants Call for proposal to bolster the security and resilience of AI systems deployed in critical infrastructure and decision-making processes. With a total funding pool of €21.2 million, this initiative aims to develop trustworthy AI models capable of withstanding adversarial manipulation, data poisoning, and unauthorized backdoor injections. Proposals should advance the state of the art in AI security by focusing on one or more of the following domains: Adversarial Robustness: Developing models that remain resilient against adversarial perturbations through techniques such as robust optimization and specialized adversarial training; Data Integrity and Detection: Implementing advanced methodologies to identify and mitigate compromised datasets, including provenance tracking and automated validation mechanisms to prevent backdoor exploitation; and Private AI Deployment: Utilizing privacy-enhancing technologies—such as federated learning, secure aggregation, and quantum-safe homomorphic encryption—to ensure that AI computations remain within trusted execution boundaries for sensitive enterprise and government applications. Selected projects are expected to receive between €3 million and €4 million. Call for proposals to support the development of cognitive electronic warfare systems February 24, 2026; European Defence Fund Grants ; AI Grants , Digital technologies grants , Innovation grants , Research grants , Security grants Call for proposals to advance the development of a net-centric and Cognitive Electronic Warfare (EW) system. This initiative aims to transition from traditional isolated sensors to a networked, multi-sensor approach that leverages artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced radiofrequency electronics. By introducing a cognitive layer, the system will enable faster decision-making and automated threat responses, providing a decisive technical advantage in increasingly contested maritime environments. A budget of EUR 24,000,000 has been allocated to support this development action. By fostering collaboration across the European naval industry, this effort seeks to strengthen the EU’s strategic autonomy and technological superiority. The project aligns with the STEP objectives for deep and digital technologies, aiming to: Enhance Interoperability: Increase commonality and interchangeability among European naval fleets and defense industries; Improve Maintenance: Utilize AI to enhance the operability and maintainability of EW systems throughout their life cycle, thereby reducing long-term costs; and Reduce Dependencies: Decrease reliance on external navigation signals and third-country technologies, ensuring an independent European response to national and regional strategic trends. Call for proposals to support the development of an AI framework for military decision-making and training February 20, 2026; European Defence Fund Grants ; AI Grants , Digital technologies grants , Innovation grants , Research grants , Security grants Call for proposals to develop a robust AI-system framework dedicated to advancing military Modelling and Simulation (M&S). This initiative seeks to create a unified, scalable environment that integrates historical datasets, doctrinal models, and synthetic training environments to provide near real-time tactical intelligence. By automating wargaming scenarios and Course of Action (COA) development, the framework aims to significantly reduce the time and costs associated with operational planning and force readiness. The call focuses on bridging current research gaps and maturing AI applications within a multi-national defense context. Key technical requirements include: Advanced AI Integration: Utilizing state-of-the-art methods such as reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, and multi-agent systems to create dynamic, adaptive simulation models; Decision Support: Developing tools that support Command and Control (C2) applications, mission execution, and instructor support for training systems; Standardization and Interoperability: Ensuring all solutions comply with NATO standards and common AI ethics frameworks to allow for seamless collaboration between EU Member States and coalition partners; and Modular Testbeds: Establishing high-performance simulation environments and a library of pre-trained agents to serve as a proving ground for novel tactical concepts. The project has a total funding allocation of EUR 16,000,000, with individual awards ranging up to EUR 8,000,000. Call for proposals to enhance soldier protection by leveraging AI and advanced robotics to provide accurate tactical awareness, building upon previous research in threat detection February 19, 2026; European Defence Fund Grants ; AI Grants , Innovation grants , Security grants Call for proposals to advance AI-driven tactical situational awareness for ground applications. With a total budget of EUR 23,000,000 and an award range of up to EUR 4,600,000 per project, this initiative seeks to protect soldiers by deploying coordinated swarms of robots and drones capable of detecting and neutralizing threats in complex environments. Selected consortia will work over a 48-month timeline to bring technologies up to Technical Readiness Level (TRL) 6, utilizing a common testing environment to ensure objective performance measurements. Proposals must integrate cutting-edge components to create a unified tactical picture, specifically addressing: Autonomous Swarm Deployment: Coordinated data gathering using multiple unmanned aerial and ground platforms; Real-Time Sensor Fusion: Integrating visual, radar, acoustic, and environmental data into a single operational interface; AI-Driven Analysis: Utilizing machine learning to prioritize threats and adapt to dynamic environmental changes like weather or obstacles; and Human-Machine Interaction: Developing intuitive interfaces that suggest automated actions for operator validation.
